summary: End-to-end tested Sveti Stefan property + PDF exposé feature. Found and FIXED a critical bug: GET /api/properties/pdf/{id} was returning 404 for the Šipkov Krš villa because the Content-Disposition header contained the Unicode 'Š' character which cannot be encoded in latin-1 (HTTP header requirement) — Starlette raised UnicodeEncodeError which the endpoint's bare `except Exception` masked as 'PDF not found'. Fixed by using RFC 5987 encoding (filename* utf-8''<encoded> + ascii fallback). After fix: PDF downloads correctly (8,248,877 bytes = ~7.9MB, magic bytes %PDF-1.7). Verified 11/11 backend pytest cases and all 6 frontend/integration test items in the request pass. Also improved the endpoint to log the underlying exception instead of silently 404ing.

minor.issue: PRE-FIX bug: Content-Disposition header used raw title with unicode chars (Š) → UnicodeEncodeError swallowed by bare `except Exception` → returned 404. FIXED in this iteration (RFC 5987 encoded filename + ascii fallback + error logging).

action_items: Consider applying the same RFC 5987 filename encoding pattern anywhere else in the codebase where property/lead/article titles may end up in a Content-Disposition header.

Replace remaining bare `except Exception: raise HTTPException(404)` blocks in routes/properties.py with logging (e.g., serve_property_image line ~108-111) so future encoding/GridFS issues surface in logs immediately.

rca of the issue: The Šipkov Krš property has title 'Šipkov Krš - Exclusive Luxury Villa' with non-latin-1 chars (Š). The old serve_property_pdf used `f'inline; filename="{prop.get("title")}.pdf"'` directly in a header value. Starlette's Response encoder does `header_value.encode('latin-1')` which raised `UnicodeEncodeError: 'latin-1' codec can't encode character '\u0160' in position 18`. The endpoint wrapped everything in `except Exception: raise HTTPException(404, 'PDF not found')` which masked the real error and made the feature look like a data-missing issue. Fix: use RFC 5987 format — `filename="<ascii-safe>.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded>.pdf` — and log the underlying exception before raising 404. Reproduction: `curl https://<host>/api/properties/pdf/6a5f5cd5f3b13d9e661f027b` returned 404 before fix, returns 200 with 8.2MB PDF after fix. Verified via pytest and Playwright end-to-end.
